source.title: Unsupervised Latent Space Alignment with Hyperspherical Geodesic Matching
source.authors: Cameron J. Ryan; V. Narayanaswamy; Kowshik Thopalli; Shu-Sen Liu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether independently trained latent spaces can be aligned using model stitching and embedding-translation evaluations, but uses HGA's geodesic-kernel alignment rather than the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The paper measures alignment outcomes for model stitching and word-embedding translation. It does not test convergence as models scale or cross-modal vision-language convergence as both models improve. Other-work findings in the related-work section are not recorded as rows. Appendix figures report additional outcomes; plotted point values not stated in the text are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study reports stitching accuracy for orthogonal maps between independently trained identical-architecture models, found with and without anchors, plus English–French FastText mapping with few anchors. This bears on V4's claim that simple maps work, even without paired data. It is largely a methods paper, and V1–V3 and V5–V7 are not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that HGA's orthogonal geodesic-kernel fit matches supervised alignment with little or no supervision on simple datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10). Optimization is unstable but can be checked through the objective score. Complex spaces (CLIP, FastText) often still need anchors. They hypothesise that latent geometries carry signatures unique up to the data, and that how useful these are for alignment depends on how little symmetry is present.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an orthogonal transformation optimized to maximize a cross-space geodesic Gaussian-kernel fit, with bandwidth continuation and random restarts. This is an alignment-utility study, not a direct scale-convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: HGA outcomes are reported as sensitive to hyperparameters. The text reports a strong objective-score/stitching-accuracy correlation at σ approximately 0.2 in the high-score regime, while at larger σ a high score is necessary but insufficient. The paper also reports different outcomes across datasets and layers.

fits_no_version.finding: HGA optimization is highly unstable: small hyperparameter changes have large effects on stitching accuracy. The objective score predicts accuracy only at σ≈0.2 in the high-score regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised geometry-based alignment of latent spaces depends on optimizer hyperparameters and has many false local optima.

fits_no_version.finding: Kernel sums after aligning DINO-V2 to CLIP-image embeddings pick out text-related THINGS concepts (banner, pennant, scoreboard) as least matched. Kernel sums also flag a class missing from one MNIST model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-alignment kernel sums can localise regions present in one model's representation but not another's, such as text-related concepts in CLIP.

record.problems: The paper reports instability and strong hyperparameter sensitivity. Model architectures and sizes are not stated for the stitching pairs. Several appendix outcomes are presented only in figures, with no exact values in the text; the text does not give the correlation coefficients or the individual hyperparameter-variation results.
record.rows_left_out: Individual plotted values across anchor counts in Figure 1, individual points in Figure 3, and individual trials in Figure 4 are not separately transcribed because their numeric values are not stated in the text. Figure 6's per-query scores and full ranked-neighbor lists are not individually transcribed; the caption-level comparison is recorded in r17–r18.

untested.parts: No scale, capability or data sweep, and no comparison across architectures or objectives.
No paired image-caption vision-language comparison. DINO-V2 vs CLIP-image is image-to-image.
Seed pairs are used but shared features, subspaces or units are not analysed.

Loss relative to native unstitched model accuracy is not reported. Not tested: cross-architecture stitching, non-matching layers, affine maps and relative representations. FastText accuracies are figure-only.
No neuron, SAE feature or circuit comparison.
No comparison of similarity measures, neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of plateaus, of how complete alignment is beyond stitching, or of shared data or objectives as the cause.

missing.what: Statement that for complex spaces such as CLIP embeddings and FastText, anchors are often still needed; no CLIP stitching numbers are given.
Missing-class detection: kernel sums for the excluded '0' class are much lower under several alignment methods (figure-only).
Per-query ranks of the correct translation for HGA and LFM: HGA bird 7, horse 2, flower 3, forest 1; LFM forest 4, others not in top 10.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a methods paper, and its evidence on V4 is indirect. Stitching is always benchmarked against a supervised orthogonal map, never against native model accuracy. All stitched pairs are identical architectures, and architecture and size are unstated. The reader's V6 links were wrong: hyperparameter sensitivity of an alignment optimizer is not dependence of measured convergence on the metric. Table 2 values are best-of-search on the test outcome and should not be used as evidence.

versions.untested_parts: No model size, capability, or training-scale sweep; no comparison of differently scaled independently trained models.
No paired image-caption vision-language representation comparison or measure of alignment changing with both models' performance.
The paper aligns identical-architecture model pairs, but does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds, or whether individual units or bases differ.

Tests orthogonal alignment for model stitching and word-embedding translation. Does not test stitching across arbitrary layers or architectures, relative representations, or alignment without paired data in all settings.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Reports sensitivity to HGA bandwidth and other hyperparameters, but does not compare multiple reasonable representation-similarity measures or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment instead of a common model of reality, or whether alignment plateaus as models scale.

rows.value: The text describes accuracy as nearly unchanged even with up to 85% of anchors corrupted.
rows.note: The paper gives a qualitative description but no numerical accuracy values in the text.

rows.subject: FastText English and French word-embedding spaces
rows.operation_detail: Compare nearest French neighbors returned after alignment for anchor and unanchored English query words.

conditions.value: dog, house, bird, horse, flower, forest

rows.measure: nearest French-neighbor retrieval and rank of correct translation
rows.baseline: LFM results are separately reported in r18
rows.value: For anchor words dog and house, the correct translation ranks first; for unanchored bird, horse, flower, and forest, the text says HGA still recovers the correct translation.
rows.note: The figure contains per-query ranked neighbors and scores; the extracted layout is flattened, so this records the paper's caption-level summary rather than reconstructing every score.
rows.check: The caption overstates the result. Figure 6 ranks HGA's correct translation 1st only for forest; it is 7th for bird (oiseau), 2nd for horse (cheval) and 3rd for flower (fleur).

source_check.correct: HGA correct-translation ranks: dog 1; house 1; bird 7; horse 2; flower 3; forest 1. Both methods receive 100 anchors.
source_check.problem: The visible value is consistent with the figure. The verdict-fix annotation incorrectly implies that the caption claims first-rank retrieval for unanchored words.

relation.reason: The study measures whether orthogonal mappings enable useful communication between independently trained latent spaces, including without anchors.

tranche.reason: Geodesic-kernel optimization provides a different alignment method whose stitching and translation results test V4.

source_check.notes: The pack truncates r17's value after bird; only its visible content can be checked. Supervised mapping accuracy is the stitching comparator, so loss relative to native model accuracy remains unmeasured.

statements.correction: Table 1: MNIST unsupervised HGA 96.55 ± 0.09%, supervised orthogonal mapping 96.79%; CIFAR-10 72.80 ± 0.30%, supervised 73.48%. Identical-architecture model pairs; 1024 alignment samples; no anchor supervision for unsupervised HGA; 50 restarts; mean and standard deviation over 3 runs. Table 1 stitching layer unspecified. Native unstitched accuracy not reported.
statements.problem: The HGA accuracies are correct, but the study does not identify Table 1 as last-layer stitching. Disjoint source/target inputs or separately sampled unpaired pools are not established.
